title: Descent of a generic polynomial hypersurface to base sections
statement: Let S be integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] and affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let eta be a generic point, meaning its closure is all of S. Put A=\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S) and K=\kappa(eta), the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. For every n and Q\in K[t_1,\ldots,t_n] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], there exists P\in A[t_1,\ldots,t_n] such that, writing H=\operatorname{Spec}(A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(P)) and g:H\to S for the coefficient-induced map followed by the inverse of the affine spectrum identification, there is an isomorphism i:H_{eta}\to\operatorname{Spec}(K[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(Q)) commuting with the two maps to \operatorname{Spec}(K). The fibre is scheme-theoretic [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. There are no nonzero, irreducibility or reducedness assumptions on Q, and no claim about fibres away from eta.

source.place: Tag 0559 (more-morphisms.tex, lemma-geom-irreducible-generic-fibre), first proof, clearing finitely many coefficient denominators in the generic fraction field

proof.text: Identify eta with the canonical generic point. Mathlib functionField_isFractionRing_of_isAffineOpen identifies Gamma(S,top) with a subring of the generic stalk fraction field. The stalk is a field; its residue map is bijective. An algebra equivalence induced by that map and IsFractionRing.of_algEquiv give the fraction-ring structure on kappa(eta) under the evaluation map.

Apply IsLocalization.exist_integer_multiples to Q.support and its coefficient function. Write each multiplied coefficient as a base section, and sum the monomials over that same finite support to form P. MvPolynomial.map_monomial, smul_monomial and support_sum_monomial_coeff show P_K=dQ. This also covers the zero polynomial, empty support and zero variables.

Use tensorQuotientEquiv to tensor the quotient, and MvPolynomial.algebraTensorAlgEquiv to identify the polynomial tensor product. Ideal.map_span and map_map identify the extended principal ideal with (P_K). The scalar d is a unit by IsLocalization.map_units, so Ideal.span_singleton_mul_left_unit identifies this ideal with (Q). Compose the two algebra equivalences.

The evaluation map describes fromSpecResidueField followed by isoSpec.hom, by fromSpecStalk_toSpecGamma and contravariance of Spec. Transport the fibre pullback across isoSpec with pullback.map, swap its factors, and apply pullbackSpecIso. Apply Spec to the inverse algebra equivalence from the preceding step. Its algebra commutation and pullbackSpecIso_hom_fst prove that the resulting scheme isomorphism commutes with the generic projection to Spec kappa(eta).

lean.statement:
theorem exists_base_hypersurface_of_generic_polynomial
    {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S] [IsIntegral S]
    (η : S) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ)
    {n : ℕ} (Q : MvPolynomial (Fin n) (S.residueField η)) :
    ∃ P : MvPolynomial (Fin n) Γ(S, ⊤),
      let H := Spec (.of (MvPolynomial (Fin n) Γ(S, ⊤) ⧸ Ideal.span {P}))
      let g : H ⟶ S := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
        ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {P})).comp MvPolynomial.C)) ≫ S.isoSpec.inv
      let Z := Spec (.of (MvPolynomial (Fin n) (S.residueField η) ⧸ Ideal.span {Q}))
      let q : Z ⟶ Spec (.of (S.residueField η)) := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
        ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {Q})).comp MvPolynomial.C))
      ∃ i : g.fiber η ≅ Z, i.hom ≫ q = g.fiberToSpecResidueField η
